summary: Explains Virtual Assets, which strip editor bulk data (e.g. raw texture source) out of .uasset files and store it in Perforce plus a shared DDC to cut sync time and disk use; covers requirements, DefaultEngine.ini setup, backend graphs and rollout strategies.
gotchas: Requires Perforce source control integration
Disabled by default
Editor cannot continue if a payload pull fails; only retry or quit
Not recommended without reliable internet access to the shared cache

summary: Step-by-step setup of Virtual Assets for a test project: Perforce plus shared DDC prerequisites, the DefaultEngine.ini backend graph, virtualizing on submit or with UnrealVirtualizationTool, and verifying via tooltip or DumpPackagePayloadInfo.
gotchas: Needs Perforce with the in-editor check-in workflow
Needs a shared Derived Data Cache

summary: Describes exporting cooked output from Zenserver as snapshots (to Unreal Cloud DDC, another Zenserver or a file archive) from build graphs, and importing them locally with ushell so you can stage/deploy without recooking.
gotchas: Requires Zenserver enabled as cooked output store first
Without Horde env vars successive snapshots duplicate more data
Incremental cook on top of an imported snapshot is listed as future

summary: Shows how to stream cooked data from a workstation's Zenserver to a target device instead of staging .pak/.utoc/.ucas containers, including config to allow remote access, editor/ushell staging options, runtime override flags and how to verify streaming is active.
gotchas: Zenserver is unauthenticated: use only on trusted LAN/VPN
Only for non-shipping configurations
Requires Zenserver as cooked output store
Avoid WiFi; use wired 1-10 Gbps or USB 3.2 Gen2

summary: Explains opting in to storing cook output inside Zenserver instead of loose files in Saved/Cooked, where the data lives on disk, garbage collection via ue.projectstore, the Zen Dashboard, and how staging to containers or loose files behaves afterwards.
keys: Use Zenserver as cooked output store
gotchas: Off by default; needs Use Io Store enabled
Saved/Cooked will no longer contain .uasset/.ubulk/.uexp files
Cooked data is evicted if ue.projectstore is deleted or older than 14 days
Put Zen data on a fast local drive, not network or virtual drives

summary: Blueprint walkthrough (HoloLens example) for spawning content pinned to real-world ARPins, saving them to the device's local store, removing them, and reloading them in a later session.
keys: Remove All ARPins from Local Store
gotchas: Written for an earlier engine version
Local store only supported on certain platforms (Windows Mixed Reality, some OpenXR extension plugins)
Requires a project set up for AR

summary: Overview of ARPins for anchoring virtual content to real-world locations, with a platform table for local and cloud persistence and pointers to Azure Spatial Anchors, ARCore Cloud Anchors and ARKit Geo Anchors APIs.
gotchas: Azure Spatial Anchors requires an Azure account
Local storage support varies by platform

summary: Reference of predefined BuildGraph XML tasks and their parameters (Compile, Cook, Stage, PakFile, Copy, Zip, Spawn, Commandlet, Zen snapshot tasks, Horde/Docker/AWS tasks, etc.) plus how to write a custom task class with TaskElement/TaskParameter.
Short VR how-to: parent meshes, effects or UI to the Pawn's Camera component so they follow the HMD, and read the camera's world location to get the player/HMD position.
gotchas: Written for UE4

summary: Shows how to display a texture as an HMD loading screen during level transitions using Set/Show/Hide Loading Screen Blueprint nodes with Load Stream Level.
gotchas: Media Framework playback is not supported in XR loading screens
Scale must be nonzero to see the texture
A short Delay after Show Loading Screen may be needed

summary: Hub page for OpenXR Stereo Layers (HMD textures rendered in a separate pass without post-processing); links to the overview and quick start.
Explains reading the user's VR play area (stage) bounds with Get Play Area Bounds and how the VR Template's VRTeleportVisualizer draws them with a Niagara system during teleport.
gotchas: Returns no data if the OpenXR runtime does not implement play area bounds

summary: Lists what to install and enable to use OpenXR with Windows Mixed Reality, Oculus or SteamVR devices, and how to pick a runtime when several are installed.
gotchas: Disable the Oculus, SteamVR and Windows Mixed Reality plugins when using the OpenXR plugin

summary: Builds a minimal AR project from the Blank template: AR Utilities plugin, empty level, ARPawn with camera, ARGameMode, an ARSessionConfig data asset and Start/Stop AR Session nodes.
gotchas: Default level sky/fog objects overlay everything in AR, so start from an empty level

summary: Near-empty intro page stating that VR performance matters for comfort and that UE has CPU/GPU profiling tools; no specific steps.

Walks through Lyra's AnimBP_Mannequin_Base: thread-safe animation update with Property Access, Anim Node Functions, state aliases, upper/lower body layering, linked anim layers per weapon, distance matching, stride and orientation warping, turn in place and debugging tools.
gotchas: Thread-safe functions cannot read game objects directly; use Property Access
Turn Yaw Anim Modifier needs Root Motion enabled on the source animation
Montage Blend Profiles plus Inertialization together not supported (stated for 5.0)

summary: Documents the CommonUser plugin from Lyra that wraps Online Subsystem/Online Services for user login, privileges and session host/find/join via UCommonUserSubsystem and UCommonSessionSubsystem, plus install steps and switching to OSSv2.
gotchas: Not designed for Blueprint-only projects
Online Services (OSSv2) is beta
Lyra defaults to the Null subsystem (editor/LAN only)

summary: Explains how Lyra registers Enhanced Input mapping configs per Game Feature, gates them by platform traits, stores them in ULyraSettingsLocal, and applies settings like gamepad sensitivity through custom Input Modifiers.
gotchas: Mappings only activate when their Game Feature is active and platform conditions are met

summary: Describes Lyra's split between inventory items (definitions with fragments, tag-stack state, owned by the controller) and equipment (spawned actors and granted abilities on the pawn), with key classes, pickups, quick bar and reticle UI.
gotchas: Only one weapon can be equipped on a character at a time
Equipment instances keep no state between equip/unequip

summary: Explains Lyra's interaction framework: a GAS interact ability with line-trace ability tasks that find actors implementing IInteractableTarget, gather FInteractionOption entries, and trigger abilities via event gameplay tags.
gotchas: InteractionScanRate radius should exceed InteractionRange or the granted ability won't replicate to the client in time

summary: Covers Lyra's GameSettings plugin for building an options menu in C++: settings registry, setting value classes, dynamic getters/setters, edit conditions (platform traits, primary player) and the UI panel classes.
gotchas: Every setting needs a unique DevName and a DisplayName
Getter/setter targets must be exposed as UFUNCTION/UPROPERTY

summary: Explains how CVars, scalability groups, device profiles, GameUserSettings and texture LOD groups combine, the CVar priority order, and how to override engine defaults in DefaultScalability.ini/DefaultEngine.ini/DefaultDeviceProfiles.ini, with Lyra's own config as the example.
gotchas: Device profile settings override user-chosen scalability groups
Device Profiles editor does not save until you use Save as Defaults to DefaultDeviceProfiles.ini
Cannot define different scalability groups per device profile
Texture group settings can't be changed at runtime

summary: Reference of Lyra's main menu, game modes (Control, Elimination, Exploder) and every options-menu setting: display, graphics quality, frame rate limits, audio, subtitles, sensitivity, key bindings, gamepad and deadzones.
General steps for upgrading a C++ game to a new engine release using Lyra as the example, plus Lyra change logs for 5.0.2 through 5.3 (TObjectPtr changes, Iris, init-state components, replays).
gotchas: Change notes stop at 5.3

summary: Tutorial for getting Lyra working with Epic Online Services: Dev Portal product/client/EAS setup, source-built engine, EOS config in Config/Custom/EOS, DevAuthTool login for two test accounts, and packaging LyraGameEOS.
gotchas: Requires an engine built from source; launcher engine cannot package LyraGameEOS
Needs two Epic accounts with 2FA
Launcher-downloaded Lyra won't work with EOS without extra setup

summary: How to add left/right Motion Controller components with child static meshes to a VR pawn and use the component's Visualization options to show device models.
gotchas: Static mesh must be a child of the Motion Controller component to follow it

summary: Setup for Oculus headsets: install the Oculus app, allow Unknown Sources, enable the Oculus VR plugin, and where to find its project settings.
gotchas: Oculus app must be running to view the plugin settings

summary: Short page on installing Steam and launching SteamVR so UE projects can run on SteamVR headsets.
gotchas: SteamVR must stay running while viewing projects
Written for UE4

summary: Quick steps to add a Stereo Layer component under the VR Template pawn's camera, assign a texture and Quad Layer shape, and verify it in the headset.
Describes OpenXR Stereo Layer types (face/tracker/world-locked), shapes, draw-order rules and component properties.
gotchas: Stereo layers don't appear in the desktop VR Preview window
Only Quad shape guaranteed on all OpenXR runtimes
Supports Depth not supported by OpenXR
Mixing face-locked priorities with other layers via vr.StereoLayers.bMixLayerPriorities is unsupported

summary: Sets up a minimal mobile/HMI project: disable unneeded plugins in the .uproject, set editor scalability to Low, and choose a mobile Preview Platform.
gotchas: Editor scalability settings do not affect final builds
Disabled features can reduce imported asset fidelity

summary: Stub noting that Pixel Streaming frontend customization docs moved to the Pixel Streaming Infrastructure repository, and that the frontend became a TypeScript library in 5.2.
